b1-need-want.title: Need/Want: мӕ ... хъӕуы
b1-need-want.explanation: To say you need or want something, Ossetian puts the experiencer (мӕ, "to me") before the thing needed, and хъӕуы ("is needed/wanted") after it: Дон мӕ хъӕуы literally means "water to-me is-needed", i.e. "I'm thirsty" / "I need water". This is the same pattern you've already seen with possession (мӕ телефон, "my phone") and negation (нӕй) -- Ossetian keeps reusing a small set of building blocks in new combinations.
b1-need-want.fact: The corpus this course draws from also shows a second, different-looking construction (an allative suffix -мӕ attached directly to the noun, as in "Скутермӕ хъӕуы" for "I want a scooter") -- that's a materially different pattern from this one and isn't taught yet, to avoid mixing up two constructions that look similar but work differently.
